app.title: GC–EI–MS Annotation Tool
app.summary: A person chooses whether to analyse one spectrum or a batch, downloads a CSV template, and pastes or uploads peak lists of mass-to-charge and intensity. They can pick a stricter or looser confidence-screening rule before they submit. The tool compares each spectrum against a fixed reference library, ranks the closest library candidates by weighted cosine similarity, and adds a model score for how reliable the top match is. It then says whether the top match meets the chosen rule. The person reads the ranked candidates, or a one-line summary per spectrum for a batch, and downloads the results as CSV files that record which library and model were used.

task.text: Find tentative compound matches for unknown mass spectra in a reference library, and flag which top matches are reliable enough to report.

data.text: Mass spectra already extracted from an instrument, each a list of ion peaks (m/z and intensity), searched against a fixed reference library of spectra with compound identities.
data.item: one mass spectrum: its ion peaks, identified by a spectrum ID in a batch

stage.text: annotating unknown compounds from extracted spectra, before confirming them with standards

mechanism.text: A mode switch decides whether a paste or upload form takes one spectrum or a batch CSV, with a screening-rule selector beside it. When the form is submitted, the engine runs and the results appear below the form: three headline numbers and a top-10 candidate table for one spectrum, or a table with one row per spectrum for a batch. Each result view has CSV downloads.

field.text: EI mass-spectral library matching for GC–MS compound annotation in analytical chemistry

workflow.name: match unknown items against a reference library and flag the confident matches

steps.here: choose Single spectrum or Batch spectra, download the matching CSV template, then paste an m/z,intensity peak list or upload a CSV (spectrum_id,mz,intensity for a batch)

steps.step: set the rule that decides which results count as confident
steps.here: an optional selector picks Standard (score ≥0.87) or Strict (score ≥0.94 and top-two margin ≥0.20); this changes which results are flagged, not the ranking

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: the peaks are binned to nominal mass and weighted by m/z × √intensity, then compared by cosine with every reference entry and ranked; a 12-feature gradient-boosting model scores how likely the top hit agrees with its library label

for one spectrum, the top candidate's similarity, agreement score and top-two difference are shown as metrics, along with a pass/fail screening status and a top-10 table of candidates with their formulas and connectivity IDs

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: for a batch, a table gives each spectrum's top candidate, formula, similarity, reliability score and whether it meets the screening rule
download the result summary, the top-10 candidate table or the batch results as CSV files, each carrying the software version and the SHA-256 checksums of the library and model

distinctive: Ranking and confidence are kept apart: similarity sets the order, and a separate model only scores whether the top hit is reliable, so the confidence score never reorders candidates.
Two preset screening rules flag results for follow-up. One uses a score threshold alone; the other also requires a minimum gap between the first and second matches.
Every export records the checksums of the source library, the reference index and the model, so a result can be traced to the exact assets that produced it.
Matches are made only at the connectivity level (the first 14 characters of the InChIKey) and are labelled tentative throughout. Retention-index data are refused rather than used.
